product.category: Flow-first programming language and developer toolchain
product.summary: An expression-oriented language with explicit data flow, a Python reference runtime, a developing native C17 track and a Windows desktop studio.
proof_points: Readable expression-oriented syntax with explicit value flow.
Python reference interpreter, CLI and language tests.
A developing native C17 core and Reaper Studio desktop surface.
non_claims: The native C17 track must not be presented as complete where project contracts mark it as developing.
Do not claim production readiness, performance superiority or ecosystem scale without comparative evidence.
Market demand, paid conversion and profitability are not established.

audiences.need: Understand a compact flow-first model with visible execution semantics.
audiences.value: A reference runtime, examples and inspectable language documentation.

audiences.need: Study and extend a language implementation with explicit contracts.
audiences.value: A Python reference path and a separately described native-development track.

audiences.need: Demonstrate expression flow, parsing and execution boundaries.
audiences.value: Runnable examples and precise distinctions between implemented and planned surfaces.

positioning.statement: Reaper is a flow-first language and toolchain for developers who want readable expressions and explicit data flow.
differentiators: Python reference runtime and CLI provide an inspectable implementation path.
The native C17 development track is distinguished from the reference runtime.
Language behaviour, resource limits and integrations are documented as explicit contracts.

brand.promise: Make program flow explicit and language behaviour inspectable.

stages.name: Problem discovery
stages.success_criteria: Collect concrete tasks from language learners and toolchain builders.

stages.name: Message and documentation
stages.success_criteria: README, language documentation and examples describe current implementation surfaces.

stages.name: Distribution
stages.success_criteria: Public source repository provides the inspectable project and build instructions.

stages.name: User validation
stages.success_criteria: Evaluate examples and first-run experience with target developers.

stages.name: Retention and support
stages.success_criteria: Maintain versioned language docs, diagnostics guidance and issue triage.

channels.name: GitHub repository and documentation
channels.purpose: Explain syntax, runtime choice, architecture and maturity boundaries.
channels.guardrail: Never imply that a developing backend is a finished stable compiler.

channels.name: Runnable examples and tutorials
channels.purpose: Help users reach a first successful program quickly.
channels.guardrail: Examples must run on the documented runtime and version.

channels.name: Technical demonstrations
channels.purpose: Show real language programs, diagnostics and explicit data flow.
channels.guardrail: Use reproducible source and publish environment details.

channels.name: Programming-language communities
channels.purpose: Collect structured feedback on syntax, semantics and tooling.
channels.guardrail: Avoid inflated ecosystem, adoption or benchmark claims.

market_validation.notes: No structured adoption or user-demand evidence is asserted.

pricing.notes: No pricing model or paid edition is defined.

unit_economics.notes: Maintenance and distribution costs require measurement.

licensing.notes: Review Apache-2.0 obligations and dependency notices for every distribution bundle.

support.notes: Define language-version support, bug triage and compatibility policy.

distribution.notes: The public source repository and build documentation are available; packaged release status is release-specific.

metrics.name: First successful program
metrics.definition: Share of evaluators who run a documented example successfully.
metrics.source: Consent-based usability sessions or explicit issue reports.
metrics.privacy_note: Do not introduce hidden editor telemetry.

metrics.name: Example completion
metrics.definition: Pass rate of documented examples against the supported reference runtime.
metrics.source: Automated example checks and CI results.

metrics.name: Issue resolution
metrics.definition: Time from reproducible language issue to verified fix or documented decision.
metrics.privacy_note: Avoid inferring adoption from repository stars alone.

governance.claims: Distinguish the Python reference runtime, native C17 development track and desktop editor maturity in every product message.
governance.promotion: Use runnable examples and source-linked demonstrations; no unsupported claims of speed, production-readiness or ecosystem adoption.
governance.privacy: Do not add undisclosed usage telemetry or collect source code from users.
governance.rights: Preserve license notices and review bundled dependencies, fonts, icons and sample code.
